signal.title: PAN3612 - Procurement of Housing Training and Learning Framework
signal.description: The Housing Division is required to respond to increasing regulatory expectations, including the introduction of the Competence and Conduct Standard, which comes into effect in October 2026. This standard requires social housing providers to evidence that staff have the appropriate skills, knowledge, experience, and display the right behaviours to deliver safe and effective services. The framework will enable Leicester City Council (LCC) to commission training and learning provision on an as-required basis throughout the duration of the framework. Lot 1: Accredited and Qualification-Based Learning. Lot 1 Accredited and qualification-based learning: CIH qualifications Levels 2-5 Housing Apprenticeships Housing leadership qualifications Professional membership pathways Lot 2: Non-Accredited Learning and Development. Lot 2 Non-Accredited Learning and Development: Housing Practice Tenancy management Customer service Equality and Diversity Lot 3: Leadership, Management and Organisational Development. Lot 3 Leadership, Management and Organisational Development: First-line manager programmes Senior leadership programmes Change management Strategic leadership Equality, diversity and inclusion within leadership Lot 4: Wellbeing, Safeguarding and Customer Excellence.. Lot 4 Wellbeing, safeguarding and customer excellence: Mental health Safeguarding Domestic abuse Complaint handling Conflict management

signal.title: SIC and SOC Coding of the Graduate Outcomes survey
signal.description: HESA (part of Jisc) are seeking a supplier to support the annual coding of occupational information. Following its merger with the Higher Education Statistics Agency, Jisc has retained 'HESA' as a brand name, and Jisc's functions, activities and role as the DDB are undertaken by a dedicated directorate within Jisc, operating under the HESA brand. References to HESA within the Specification do not mean any legal entity. This will include Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) and Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), along with some additional information to supplement this. The supply of this data will support our role as the designated data body for the HE sector, ensuring high quality, consistent classification of employer data. As survey responses are received, HESA/Jisc will securely make available to the supplier, in batches, an overnight file of the employer, course and role information to enable the supplier to complete the required SIC and SOC coding and return it to HESA/Jisc using an encrypted secure bulk data sending system. In addition to the purposes set out below, the coding will be used by Jisc to update and feed into the Graduate Outcomes provider dashboards so that Providers have visibility of the progress and outcomes of the coding. HESA/Jisc will run the Graduate Outcomes survey, working with third-party suppliers to manage the call centre system for contact management and to provide an online survey. It will be necessary for the supplier to join review calls with HESA/Jisc and HESA/Jisc's third-party suppliers to feedback any improvements required to the job role and employer data to improve the accuracy of coding. Lot LOT-0000: .

signal.title: PME Erasmus
signal.description: This is not a call for competition. The London Borough of Croydon is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to the potential commissioning of an Erasmus+ teacher/educator training and international mobility programme for Croydon schools. The Council is seeking expressions of interest only from organisations with demonstrable previous experience of managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects and international education mobility programmes on behalf of schools or public-sector organisations. The appointed provider would be expected to provide end-to-end programme management, including: • Previous experience of successfully managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects, including details of the number and type of projects delivered • Management and coordination of international teacher training, CPD and school visits across European destinations, with destinations to be confirmed • Organisation and management of participant travel, accommodation, and associated logistics • Support with participant recruitment and selection, including ensuring appropriate eligibility and allocation processes • Management of Erasmus+ grant administration, financial monitoring, evidence, and reporting requirements • Support for safeguarding, risk management and participant welfare throughout the programme • Delivery or commissioning of high-quality teacher CPD and training aligned to the agreed programme objectives • Development and implementation of programme evaluation, impact measurement, and outcomes reporting • Monitoring and reporting on participant outcomes and the wider impact of the programme on participating schools; and • Effective stakeholder management and communication with the Council, schools, training providers, and international partners. The programme is intended to support Croydon schools in developing practice in areas including inclusion and SEND, digital and AI-enabled education, wellbeing, sustainability, innovation, and oracy/communication-rich learning, aligned with relevant Erasmus+ priorities. Providers should only register an interest where they can demonstrate the relevant specialist experience, capacity, international networks and organisational infrastructure required to manage an Erasmus+ mobility programme from participant selection through to final evaluation and grant reporting. Registering your interest Providers wishing to participate must register their interest through the correspondence area no later than 21 September 2026 Please complete the sections provided in the document attached and return via the messaging area on the inTend Portal: Following the registration deadline, the Council will review responses and may engage with organisations whose experience and capabilities align with the requirements. This market engagement exercise is intended to inform the Council's understanding of the market and potential future commissioning arrangements. It does not constitute a procurement process, and participation does not provide any advantage in any future procurement activity. Organisation name Main contact name and job title Contact email address A brief response confirming: • the number of Erasmus+ projects your organisation has previously managed • your experience of managing international school/teacher mobility programmes • your experience of grant administration and reporting • your ability to manage travel, accommodation, participant selection, safeguarding, CPD and evaluation; and • a brief example of a comparable programme successfully delivered. Word Limit: 250 words The London Borough of Croydon use the Intend portal to manage supplier records and to run procurement activities. If you do not yet have an account, please register, if you do have an account, It is essential that your company information on Intend matches the details held by Companies House, please do log in and check this. Intend Portal: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/croydontenders/aspx/Home Register on the Central Digital Platform If you haven’t already, please register your organisation on the Central Digital Platform. This is a government-wide initiative to streamline supplier engagement and improve transparency. Again please do ensure your information matches your Companies House details. Central Digital Platform Registration: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/suppliers-how-to-register-your-organisation-and-first-administrator-on-find-a-tender-in-three-easy-steps-html We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to working together. Lot 1: . None

signal.title: Managed lettings services for The Sir John Brunner Foundation
signal.description: The Sir John Brunner Foundation Multi-Academy Trust (Cheshire) is undertaking pre-market engagement in relation to a proposed procurement for the management of community lettings and facilities hire across part of its estate. The initial scope is expected to include Middlewich High School and Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College, with the possibility of future extension to other Trust sites, subject to suitability, value for money and operational requirements. The Trust's wider estate includes The County High School, Leftwich and (from November) primary academies in the Northwich area. The Trust is seeking to understand the market for managed lettings services and to inform the development of its final specification, procurement route and commercial model. The proposed requirement is expected to involve the management, marketing, booking, administration and operational delivery of lettings and community use of school and college facilities outside core educational hours. The Trust's objectives are to: increase utilisation of facilities outside normal school and college hours; improve and expand access for local clubs, voluntary organisations and community groups; support sustainable community use, particularly for local and regular users; ensure safeguarding, site security, supervision and operational control during lettings activity; reduce the administrative and operational burden on academy staff; protect the condition, readiness and availability of facilities for core educational use; increase income through improved utilisation and broader use of facilities, rather than relying solely on price increases; and establish a professional, compliant and scalable lettings model capable of operating across multiple academy sites where appropriate. The facilities potentially within scope include, but are not limited to, indoor sports halls, outdoor pitches, all-weather/3G or astro facilities, playing fields, performance and assembly spaces, classrooms, specialist teaching areas, changing rooms, car parking and ancillary facilities. The final list of facilities will be confirmed following engagement with the market. The Trust is particularly interested in engaging with providers able to deliver one or more of the following models: a fully managed lettings service, including marketing, bookings, customer management, income collection, staffing, supervision, safeguarding, compliance and reporting; a managed bookings and staffing model, including provider-led marketing, customer management and revenue administration, with operational delivery agreed between the provider and the Trust; and/or advice on appropriate commercial structures, including revenue share, guaranteed income, management fee or hybrid models. At this stage, the Trust does not intend to pursue a software-only booking platform as the primary solution, as the requirement includes a need for operational delivery, staffing and site supervision, particularly at Middlewich High School. However, the Trust welcomes feedback on systems and technology used to support managed lettings services. The Trust anticipates that any future contract would require the successful provider to demonstrate robust arrangements for: on-site staffing and supervision; safeguarding, site security and incident escalation; access control, opening, closing and site handover; cleaning, facility reset and reporting of damage or defects; customer service and complaints management; protection and transition of existing community users where possible; pricing strategy and affordability for local community users; financial reporting, reconciliation, VAT information and income remittance; performance reporting and attendance at formal contract review meetings; and orderly exit and transfer of booking/customer data at the end of the arrangement. The Trust is considering a phased implementation approach, with Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College and non-pitch lettings at Middlewich High School potentially commencing first, followed by Middlewich High School pitch or astro lettings at a later stage to allow appropriate transition and notice for existing users. The estimated value of the initial opportunity is currently expected to be in the region of £420,000 to £480,000 or more over an initial three-year period, based on estimated gross lettings income across the sites. This estimate is indicative only and will be reviewed as the commercial model, scope and contract structure are developed. The final classification and value of any subsequent procurement will be confirmed before the formal tender stage. The purpose of this pre-market engagement is to: understand supplier capability and capacity in the managed school and college lettings market; test the proposed scope, delivery model and phasing; understand appropriate commercial models and risk allocation; identify key operational, safeguarding, staffing and financial considerations; inform the Trust's final specification and procurement documents; and ensure that any subsequent procurement is proportionate, transparent and capable of delivering best value. Participation in this pre-market engagement will not confer any advantage in any subsequent procurement process. Information shared by the Trust will be made available on a consistent basis where appropriate, and any future competition will be conducted in accordance with the Trust's procurement obligations, including the principles of transparency, equal treatment and non-discrimination. Interested providers are invited to respond to this notice and may be invited to participate in a site visit. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately, and the Trust reserves the right not to proceed to procurement following this engagement. Lot 1: .

signal.title: Mechanical & Public Health Framework (MPHF) (2026-30)
signal.description: This Prior Information Notice (PIN) relates to a project to establish a Mechanical & Public Health Framework (MPHF) (2026-30) (UOS-42409-2026) at the University of Strathclyde. Lot 4: Specialist Gases & Compressed Air Systems. This lot will include, however, will not be limited to: - specialist gas systems: design, supply, installation, & commissioning of laboratory gas systems, including oxygen (O2), nitrogen (N2), carbon dioxide (CO2), hydrogen (H2), argon (Ar), and other specialist/research gases / cylinder manifold systems & bulk gas storage / pressure regulation, changeover systems, & safety devices / medical & healthcare teaching gas systems (where applicable): - compressed air systems: supply, installation & upgrade of compressed air systems / supply, installation & maintenance of compressors, dryers, receivers, & filtration systems / distribution pipework & outlets / oil-free & medical-grade compressed air systems: - distribution infrastructure: internal pipework systems (copper, stainless steel, or specialist materials) / lab bench connections & service outlets / zoning, isolation, & emergency shut-off systems: - controls, monitoring & safety: alarm systems & leak detection / integration with Building Management Systems (BMS) where applicable / compliance with relevant safety standards & pressure system regulations; and - testing, commissioning & maintenance: pressure testing, purging, & certification of systems / planned preventative maintenance (PPM) & reactive works / system validation and performance testing.. Please note, the lot structure is still to be confirmed, and is therefore subject to change. Lot 2: Public Health. This lot will include, however, will not be limited to: - domestic water services: installation, refurbishment, & maintenance of hot and cold-water services pipework / system balancing & pressure management / dead leg removal & system optimisation: - water storage tanks: inspection, installation, replacement, and refurbishment of cold-water storage tanks: - Legionella compliance (L8 works): temperature control measures & required system modifications: - above & below ground drainage: installation, refurbishment, & maintenance of above ground & below ground drainage systems; and - thermal pipe insulation: installation & upgrade of insulation on domestic water pipework / compliance with energy efficiency & condensation control standards / identification and remediation of insulation defects.. Please note, the lot structure is still to be confirmed, and is therefore subject to change. Lot 3: Ventilation. This lot will include, however, will not be limited to: - ventilation systems: design, supply, installation, & commissioning of ventilation systems / general repairs & modifications to both supply & extract systems for teaching, office, & laboratory spaces / mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR) systems / upgrades to improve air quality and energy efficiency: - ductwork systems: supply, installation & modification of ductwork systems / fire-rated & acoustic ductwork / air distribution systems & associated components: - air handling & plant: supply & installation of air handling units (AHUs), fans, & associated plant / refurbishment & replacement of existing equipment / integration with existing systems & infrastructure: - specialist ventilation (laboratories & critical spaces): supply, installation & modification of local exhaust ventilation (LEV) systems / supply & installation of ventilation for cleanrooms, workshops, and high-risk environments; and - associated works: controls integration with Building Management Systems (BMS) / builders’ work and penetrations / testing, commissioning, & validation (e.g. air balancing, LEV testing).. Please note, the lot structure is still to be confirmed, and is therefore subject to change. Lot 5: Fume Cupboards & Safety Cabinets. signal.title: Design, Supply and Delivery of Uniform and PPE
signal.description: Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Lot 1: . Our vision is to create a fully branded, inclusive, and functional workwear and PPE solution that unites every colleague across our organisation reflecting who we are, what we stand for, and the pride we take in serving our communities. We will deliver a modern, high‐quality uniform range designed from the ground up to support the unique needs of our operational, maritime, port, and shore‐based teams. Rooted in the heritage of Caledonian MacBrayne and our communities, our workwear will combine safety, comfort, durability, and unmistakable brand identity in every garment. Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Through clear uniform standards, easy maintenance guidance, and from warehouse to home/work distribution processes, we will set and uphold a new standard for how our brand is worn and represented. Powered by digital self-service ordering tools, our workwear transformation will enhance operational efficiency, improve stock management, and allow us to scale sustainably. Cross-functional collaboration at the early stages will ensure that every voice is heard and every role is understood, creating a sense of ownership, pride, and confidence in the final solution. By learning from industry-leading transformations and working with expert partners, we will introduce a workwear range that not only serves practical needs but also strengthens culture, improves staff experience, and supports our organisation’s evolution. This is more than new uniform, it's an opportunity to reinforce our brand, celebrate our heritage, empower our people, and deliver a workwear experience that is fit for the future.

signal.title: Business Engagement Consultancy for Faculty of Health and Life Sciences- Expressions of Interest
signal.description: Expression of interest stage for future competition for provision of business consultancy services. The University is looking for a consultant (individual or company) that will will work with the Faculty of Health and Life Sciences and the Division of Research, Enterprise and Innovation to develop value propositions and service packages around relevant University capabilities to engage with potential industry partners and attract direct industry funding. They will provide business development expertise in designing those value propositions around industry need and profile and communicate the Faculty's unique assets and capabilities (e.g. expertise, data, platforms, patient access, facilities and equipment, and technical expertise) and promote investigator data packages to potential partners under appropriate confidentiality arrangements. These services will include, but are not exclusive, to engineering biology, health data science and artificial intelligence, infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance. To express an interest in this opportunity, please follow the link at the end of this notice. Please note, the University of Bristol is not a contracting authority as defined in the Procurement Act 2023 and this is not a regulated procurement exercise.

signal.title: Beauftragung einer externen sicherheitstechnischen Betreuung/Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit - SiFa
signal.description: Das Leibniz-Institut für Lebensmittel-Systembiologie an der Technischen Universität München beabsichtigt, einen Auftrag über die externe sicherheitstechnische Betreuung einschließlich der Stellung einer Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit (Sifa) gemäß den geltenden gesetzlichen Vorgaben zu vergeben. Der Auftraggeber beschäftigt derzeit rund 110 Mitarbeitende; in den kommenden zwei Jahren wird ein Anstieg auf voraussichtlich 130 Mitarbeitende erwartet. Die betriebliche Struktur umfasst neben Büro- und IT-Arbeitsplätzen insbesondere chemische und biologische Laborbereiche (Schutzstufen 1 und 2) sowie gentechnische Arbeiten der Sicherheitsstufe 1. Die Laborbereiche sind derzeit der Gefährdungsgruppe I zuzuordnen. Die Betreuung umfasst insbesondere die regelmäßige Grundbetreuung in angemessenem zeitlichem Umfang, die überwiegend durch die Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit und ergänzend durch die Betriebsärztin bzw. den Betriebsarzt erfolgt. Aufgrund der besonderen betrieblichen und wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeiten ergeben sich erhöhte Anforderungen an eine fachkundige, praxiserfahrene und rechtssichere sicherheitstechnische Betreuung. signal.title: Corporate Business Travel
signal.description: The Authority is procuring a comprehensive Corporate Travel Management Service to support the booking and management of business travel across the organisation. The project aims to appoint an innovative supplier capable of delivering a high-quality, customer-focused service through both an online booking platform and an offline support function. The service will cover rail, accommodation, air travel, and car hire, ensuring travellers and customers have timely, appropriate, and cost-effective travel arrangements. The supplier will work collaboratively with the Authority to streamline processes, support policy compliance, control costs, and provide ongoing management information to monitor spend and trends. Key requirements include a fully functional online booking system, traveller profile management, integration with third-party providers, consolidated invoicing, and extensive management reporting. The system must also provide traveller tracking capabilities, emergency support, and be available 24/7 with agreed service levels for system outages and operational response times. The contract will run for three years from March 2026, with an option to extend by one year. Additional obligations include environmental support, data security compliance (GDPR, ISO 27001), training for the Buying Team, and support for future changes such as potential moves to self-service booking. The supplier will also be required to provide an exit plan and participate in regular contract management reviews to ensure continuous improvement and performance against KPIs.
